messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: GPU queue depth spike in customer-vpc-42 — sustained 12m, 98% GPU util, pods pending due to nodeProvisionTimeouts. Severity: P1. Links: https://ops.redwood/internal/incidents/1912345678 :rotating_light:
olivia: ack, I'm oncall. grabbing recent graphs. seeing a fast ramp in queued requests to shim-vpc-42 (batching backlog).
olivia: most interesting part: autoscaler attempted 3 scale-ups but nodes are stuck in Provisioning -> FailedAttachVolume. kube events show cloud provider API errors and EC2 quota-ish errors.
drew: fyi I just saw a spike in customer support alerts for latency >= 10s and 429s from the private gateway.
matt: can someone paste the failing event?
olivia: paste: ```
Events:
  Type     Reason                 Age                 From                Message
  ----     ------                 ----                ----                -------
  Warning  FailedAttachVolume     2m (x12 over 8m)    attach-detach       Multi-Attach error for volume "vol-0abc" : incorrect state
  Warning  FailedScheduling       1m (x30 over 12m)   default-scheduler    0/12 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient GPUs, 4 NodeProvisioning, 2 Insufficient memory
```
ria: looks like two problems: (1) cluster-level GPU quota fully consumed, (2) the cloud provider is delaying attach ops causing nodes to fail readiness checks -> autoscaler keeps retrying and exhausting retries.
oncall-sre: I'm taking stage. assigning ops runbook: reduce incoming traffic, enable fallback to hosted inference, and attempt manual node creation with different AZ.
drew: how many active queued requests?
olivia: current queue snapshot (prefix requests): 14k total, 9k waiting for gpu backend, median wait ~ 8.9s. We hit per-customer hard queue limit and started throttling at gateway -> 429s.
matt: recommend mitigation steps:
1) Run temporary route-weight shift to route 30% of traffic to hosted model pool (no customer data allowed) -> reduces load on private cluster.
2) Increase node group max from 12->16 if cloud quotas allow.
3) Manually provision 2 on-demand nodes in AZ-b to avoid the bad attach behavior.
4) If attach errors persist, enable fail-open fallback to cpu-serving for short gen jobs (lower perf).
ria: i'll run 1) and open a support case with provider.
olivia: executing traffic shift now. config snippet:
```yaml
- route: customer-vpc-42
  variant_weights:
    private-vpc: 0.7
    hosted: 0.3
  rollout: immediate
```
Applying... :hourglass_flowing_sand:
oncall-sre: 👍 when traffic shift applied, monitor queue depth and pod pending count.
olivia: traffic shift applied. queued->gpu dropped from 9k to 4.6k in 40s. latency alerts clearing but still P1 because attach errors continue.
drew: customer impacted? support says a handful of high-importance customers hit retries and errors earlier. Need to prepare customer message: ETA for full restoration 2-3 hours while provider investigates.
ria: provider support replied: seeing elevated API latencies in AZ-c causing attach timeouts ~12m. They're mitigating but can't commit ETA. They suggested creating instances in AZ-b or using instance store for temporary workload.
matt: manual node create attempt: ```aws ec2 run-instances --image-id ami-xxx --subnet subnet-yyy --tag-specs 'ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=cluster,Value=private-vpc-42}]' --instance-type p4d.24xlarge```
olivia: manual create succeeded in AZ-b, kube node joined, gpu capacity +1. scaling now sees 2 more nodes ready. queued->gpu fell to 2.1k.
oncall-sre: good. keep hosted fallback active until provider confirms attach stability. also enable autoscaler cooldown to avoid thrash: set scaleDownDelay=10m, scaleUpLimit=2 per 5m.
ria: done. cooldown applied to nodegroup.
drew: we need to update incident timeline and notify affected customers + CSMs. Anyone want to draft message?
olivia: I'll draft a short message: "We experienced degraded inference capacity for private VPC due to cloud attach timeouts in AZ-c. We routed traffic to hosted pool and manually provisioned nodes in AZ-b to restore capacity. Root cause: provider API latencies causing volume attach failures. Mitigations in place; monitoring. ETA for full recovery TBD pending provider."
matt: ping infra: can we add a temporary guard in our autoscaler to prefer AZs with healthy attach metrics? That would help. Filed RFC-ops ticket.
ria: logs to include in postmortem:
- autoscaler events (scale attempts)
- kube events for FailedAttachVolume
- provider API error traces and ticket id
- timeline of traffic shift and manual node provision

oncall-sre: good. I'll run a quick sanity: check for orphaned volumes and clean up to avoid hitting quota. command: ```aws ec2 describe-volumes --filters Name=tag:cluster,Values=private-vpc-42 | jq '.Volumes[] | {VolumeId,State,Attachments}'```
olivia: execution note: we found 3 volumes in "attaching" for > 20m, provider support is cleaning them up.
drew: status update for execs in 15m with current mitigations and customer list.
olivia: thanks team. continuing to monitor. will update thread and handoff to next oncall at 1912349000 if still ongoing. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident 1912345678 status update: mitigation in progress, customer impact reduced, slack channel archived to incidents once resolved.
